wu: Students stand in a circle. Teacher says 'I can play football' and throws a soft ball to a student, who must say a true sentence about their own ability and throw the ball to another student. The game continues until everyone has spoken twice.
wuAlt: Students write down 3 things they can do and 3 they can't, then mingle and share sentences with 3 partners using 'I can/can't...'
Teacher projects 5 sports images (football, swimming, running, tennis, basketball). Students guess 'He/She can play...' for each image.
pres: Teacher shows a photo of a Moroccan athlete (e.g., Hicham El Guerrouj) and says 'He can run very fast. He could run 1500m in 3 minutes 26 seconds.' Teacher models 'can' for present ability and 'could' for past ability, highlighting the difference. Students repeat chorally and individually. Teacher asks 'What can you do now? What could you do when you were younger?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Teacher uses a timeline on the board: 'Now' and '5 years ago'. Students write sentences about their abilities in both tenses, then compare with a partner.
Teacher tells a personal story: 'When I was 10, I couldn't swim, but now I can swim well.' Students ask follow-up questions with 'Can you...?' and 'Could you...?'
prac: Students work in pairs with a 'Find someone who...' grid with sports abilities (e.g., 'can swim 50m', 'can play basketball', 'could ride a bike at age 5'). They ask 'Can you...?' or 'Could you...?' and write names. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation of 'can/could'.
pracAlt: Teacher distributes flashcards with sports and abilities. Students pick one and create a sentence (e.g., 'I can play tennis' or 'He could run fast'). They then mingle and read their sentences to others, who guess the sport.
Students play 'Ability Charades': one student mimes a sport ability (e.g., swimming), others guess 'Can you swim?' or 'Could you swim?'.
ls: Students listen to a 2-minute podcast clip where two teens talk about their sports achievements. They complete a gap-fill worksheet with sentences like 'Last year, I ___ (can/was able to) climb Mount Toubkal' and 'I ___ (can/could) swim before I ___ (can/could) ride a bike'. Teacher plays the clip twice, then reviews answers.
re: Students stand in two lines. Teacher calls out an ability (e.g., 'can jump high'). The first student in each line mimes it, and the fastest team gets a point. The game continues with different abilities.
prod: Students form groups of 3-4. Each group chooses a Moroccan sport (e.g., football, athletics, martial arts) and creates a 3-minute podcast panel discussion. They take turns saying 'I can/can't...' (present) and 'I could/couldn't...' (past), using adverbs like 'well' or 'fast'. Groups present to the class, and peers ask questions.
rw: Students read a short profile of a Moroccan athlete (e.g., Noureddine Morceli) and underline all examples of 'can/could/was able to'. Then, they write 5 sentences about their own abilities, using at least one 'could' and one 'can'.
st: Teacher tells a short story about a young Moroccan footballer who practiced hard and 'could' eventually play professionally. Students reflect on 'What abilities do you need to achieve your goals?' Class ends with the teacher saying: 'Today we talked about what we can do now and what we could do before. Thank you for your hard work! Goodbye.'
g: Teams race to write sentences on the board with 'can/could' and sports words.
Students mime sports abilities for others to guess using 'Can you...?' or 'Could you...?'
Students create bingo cards with abilities; teacher calls them out and students mark if they can do them.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a paragraph about a famous Moroccan athlete's abilities using 'could' and 'can'.
Support learners: Use sentence starters like 'I can...' and 'I could...' to guide their writing.
hw: Write a 10-12 sentence text about your sports abilities: one paragraph about now (can/can't) and one about the past (could/couldn't).
Interview a family member about their sports abilities when they were young and write 5 sentences.
Draw a timeline of your sports abilities from age 5 to now, with a sentence for each age.
tip: Use local sports heroes like Hicham El Guerrouj to make the theme culturally relevant and motivating for Moroccan learners.
